title: Ridge/Lasso Regression
description: Regularized linear regression models preventing overfitting.
name: Ridge/Lasso Regression
summary: Ridge (L2 regularization) and Lasso (L1 regularization) regression extend linear regression by adding a penalty term to the loss function. Ridge penalizes squared weights to shrink coefficients, while Lasso penalizes absolute weights, enabling feature selection by driving some coefficients to zero.
use_when: Working with linear regression models on datasets with high multicollinearity or a large number of features.
avoid_when: Non-linear relationships dominate or training speed is prioritized over coefficient control.
pros: Lasso performs automatic feature selection by zeroing out coefficients.
Ridge handles multicollinearity effectively by distributing weights.
Significantly reduces model variance compared to standard OLS.
cons: Requires careful tuning of the regularization parameter alpha.
Underperforms if the true underlying relationship is highly non-linear.
Lasso can arbitrarily select one feature from a group of highly correlated features.

key_hyperparams.name: alpha
key_hyperparams.note: Regularization strength; must be a positive float. Larger values specify stronger regularization.

quick_start:
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge, Lasso
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randn(100, 10)
y = np.random.randn(100)
ridge = Ridge(alpha=1.0).fit(X, y)
lasso = Lasso(alpha=0.1).fit(X, y)
